summary.text: At \(n=9\), the product of the first nine primes is \(223{,}092{,}870\), and \(223{,}092{,}870^2+1=29^2\cdot 59{,}180{,}057{,}841{,}661\). Thus this term is not squarefree, since the prime \(29\) occurs with multiplicity at least two, which already falsifies the conjunction regardless of the infinitude claim.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k,
\]
where \(p_0=2,p_1=3,p_2=5,\ldots\) are the primes in increasing order. Thus the sequence under consideration is
\[
a(n)=P_n^2+1.
\]
We will disprove the assertion that every \(a(n)\) is squarefree by exhibiting a prime whose square divides \(a(9)\).

The first nine primes are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_9
 &=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23\\
 &=223092870.
\end{aligned}
\]
For example, this multiplication can be grouped as
\[
(2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7)(11\cdot13)(17\cdot19\cdot23)
 =210\cdot143\cdot7429
 =223092870.
\]

Now consider the prime \(29\). It is prime because its only possible prime divisors not exceeding \(\sqrt{29}<6\) are \(2,3,5\), and none of these divides \(29\). Its square is
\[
29^2=841.
\]
The ninth primorial has the following residue modulo \(841\):
\[
223092870=841\cdot265270+800.
\]
Hence
\[
P_9\equiv800\equiv-41\pmod{841}.
\]
Squaring and adding one gives
\[
P_9^2+1\equiv(-41)^2+1=1681+1=1682=2\cdot841\equiv0\pmod{841}.
\]
Therefore
\[
29^2=841\mid P_9^2+1=a(9).
\]
For completeness, the term and the corresponding quotient are explicitly
\[
a(9)=223092870^2+1=49770428644836901
\]
and
\[
49770428644836901=841\cdot59180057841661.
\]

A positive integer is squarefree precisely when the square of no prime divides it. Since the prime square \(29^2\) divides \(a(9)\), the integer \(a(9)\) is not squarefree. Thus the universal assertion
\[
\forall n\in\mathbb N,\quad a(n)\text{ is squarefree}
\]
is false.

The proposed conjecture is the conjunction of this universal squarefreeness assertion with the assertion that \(a(n)\) is prime for infinitely many \(n\). A conjunction is false as soon as either one of its two components is false. Since its squarefreeness component already fails at \(n=9\), the full conjecture is false, irrespective of whether infinitely many terms of the sequence are prime. This supplies the required disproof.
